title: Customer network DNS weirdness — field notes and next steps
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a compact working log capturing the week of field work for AetherLabs on their VPC-connected on-prem stack. Focus: repeated intermittent name resolution failures for internal service endpoints after the install, customer-facing timeouts when calling the inference gateway, and a couple of odd TTL/round-robin behaviours. Goal: capture exact symptoms, what we tried, outstanding unknowns, and clear owners for follow-ups.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Impact: AetherLabs saw 10–40% request failure rate to the inference gateway during business hours (09:00–17:00 local) on 2026-10-02 — most failures surfaced as DNS NXDOMAIN or long (>10s) resolution times, causing client SDK retries and some duplicated requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: blended DNS cache poisoning/inconsistent split-horizon configuration across their on-prem DNS forwarders + intermittent packet loss between the primary VPC peering link and the customer-provisioned DNS proxy.
- Immediate mitigation: route critical gateway hostnames to the private /etc/hosts entry on the inference node pool (short-term), increased DNS cache TTL on our side to 60s, and enabled a fallback to regional-hosted inference endpoint for 2 of their high-volume tenants.
- Open: need packet captures from customer edge during an incident window, and confirmation of forwarder configs from their infra team. Also re-evaluate our SDK retry backoff to avoid amplification during DNS storms.

Timeline & raw notes:
2026-10-02 08:45 — Pre-install check (Riley): validated base install of 1.4.2 inference-runtime, all pods healthy, iptables rules consistent. Noted DNSsec not enforced on their forwarders.
2026-10-02 09:20 — First customer report: high failure rates from their QA microservice hitting /v1/completions; errors from SDK: "getaddrinfo: Name or service not known" or "DNS timeout". Observed spike in client-side retries.
2026-10-02 09:35 — Live debugging (Aisha + Diego): queried names from inference nodes: sometimes resolved to internal VIPs, sometimes returned NXDOMAIN. Repeated resolution (dig + trace) showed different responses depending on which forwarder was used (fw-01 vs fw-02).
2026-10-02 10:10 — Escalate to customer network team: they confirmed fw-01/02 are managed separately by two subteams; fw-02 had a recent change rolling out a new conditional-forwarding rule (supposed to be opt-in).
2026-10-02 11:00 — Temporary mitigation: patched /etc/hosts on inference nodes to pin inference-gateway.aether to the private VIP. This reduced errors for ~40 minutes but is fragile (manual and not synced across autoscaled nodes).
2026-10-03 14:00 — Observed recurrence during peak load; captured logs showing repeated TTL=0 responses coming from a middlebox. Initiated packet capture (tcpdump) on node and asked customer to capture on their edge for overlap window.
2026-10-04 09:00 — Found stale round-robin entries in customer's internal DNS cache — old VIPs that had been decommissioned but were still being returned by fw-02. Also observed ~0.3% packet loss on the L3 path during peak windows (customer monitoring).

Troubleshooting details / commands used (notes to self):
- On inference node: dig +short @127.0.0.1 inference-gateway.aether ANY ; dig +trace inference-gateway.aether
- tcpdump filter used: "udp port 53 or port 5353 or host inference-node-03" -w /tmp/dns-issue-20261003.pcap
- Observed response pattern (example):
  - fw-01 -> A 10.10.100.12 (expected VIP)
  - fw-02 -> NXDOMAIN or A 10.10.250.7 (decommissioned)
- SDK behavior: immediate retry x2 with 200ms then 500ms backoffs; leads to repeated load on DNS layer and duplicate requests to gateway when resolution flips mid-flow.

Hypotheses considered (priority order):
1) Configuration divergence between forwarders (most likely) — one forwarder still answers from stale cache or has an extra conditional forwarder rule.
2) Middlebox interfering with DNS (rare but seen on older appliances) — returns responses with modified TTLs causing cache churn.
3) Packet loss causing upstream resolver timeouts and the client fallback to different forwarder leading to inconsistent answers (amplified by aggressive retries).

Customer constraints observed:
- Firewall change window limited to 03:00–04:30 local; ops team prefers minimal host-level changes.
- Compliance: cannot add our managed DNS proxy inside their network. So long-term we need a solution that doesn't require inbound network changes.

Action items and owners (short list):
- Aisha: draft a minimal host-init script to set /etc/hosts via a DaemonSet for short term (automated, idempotent) — due 2026-10-08.
- Diego: follow up with customer fw-02 subteam, request their conditional-forwarding config dump and timestamped cache entries — due 2026-10-07. Linked JIRA-INF-4421.
- Riley: analyze PCAPs (customer-supplied + our node) for signs of middlebox tampering, flag any truncated/fragmented UDP responses — due 2026-10-09.
- Sophie: propose SDK retry tuning (exponential backoff + jitter) to reduce amplification; create small A/B test plan — due 2026-10-12 (JIRA-OPS-3172).
- Product / Sales sync: decide if we expose a supported documented workaround for customers with split-forwarder setups (A/B: our hosts override vs recommended forwarder config). Product to own messaging (check with Kate in product-hosted-api).

Risks / notes for leadership:
- Manual /etc/hosts fixes are brittle and do not scale with autoscaling or multi-region deployments. Need automation and a clear deprecation timeline.
- If the underlying issue is a middlebox actively rewriting DNS responses, that can affect pathing and caching at L7 and lead to potential data leakage if the fake answers point outside the expected VPC. Escalate quickly if proof appears.

Meeting snippets (raw):
- Diego: "It behaves like we had seen with the old netgear boxes — some devices are responding with NXDOMAIN when they see unknown qnames. Not a full poison but a partial rule set leak."
- Customer lead (Aether infra): "We rolled fw-02 change at 02:00 last week; didn't expect this. We'll dump the forwarders and search for old zones."
- Sophie: "SDK change is low risk and buys time — reduce client side retries to 1 by default and add jitter. Avoid immediate replays."

Docs & references embedded here:
- internal runbook: confluence://private-deploys/field-runbook-v2 (see DNS troubleshooting -> section 4)
- related tickets: JIRA-INF-4421 (customer DNS investigation), JIRA-OPS-3172 (SDK retry tuning), NOTE: cross-reference INF-3989 (old: middlebox DNS anomalies).

Outstanding questions (for follow-up):
- Can the customer share timestamped resolver logs (query + reply) for an incident window? we need to correlate to our node captures.
- Are there any HA devices (load balancers) on their side that rewrite DNS answers for geo routing?
- Do they have a DNS cache purging mechanism we can trigger remotely?

Next immediate steps (this week):
1) Push the automated hosts DaemonSet to the customer's cluster (opt-in, reversible). Aisha to coordinate with field PM for roll-out notes.
2) Riley + Diego to complete PCAP analysis and submit a short findings note (attach as pcap excerpt).
3) Sophie to prepare SDK patch and small rollout plan (canary to 5% of traffic).
4) Schedule a 30-minute network sync with customer fw-02 subteam for 2026-10-09 10:00 (send calendar invite after Diego confirms availability).

Quick appendix (operational checklist for engineers):
- How to capture: sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/dns-dump-$(date +%Y%m%d).pcap port 53 or port 5353
- How to inspect: tshark -r /tmp/dns-dump.pcap -Y dns -V | less ; or use Wireshark with DNS coloring
- How to temporarily pin host (not recommended long-term): echo "10.10.100.12 inference-gateway.aether" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts && systemctl restart inference-agent

Notes to self: keep pressure on the customer to share resolver logs; without that the hypothesis remains high-confidence but unproven. Also, take a close look at our CDN/resolver timeouts — if we can tolerate slightly longer upstream timeouts, some of the tail failures disappear.

-- end of working log --
(append additional PCAP summary + small screenshots to the confluence page linked above once Riley finishes analysis)
